active_protagonist.evidence: The spine says: 'At Daksha's tapasya she promises to be born his daughter and Shiva's wife, and she sets her own condition.'

crisis_from_flaw.evidence: The spine says: 'When Daksha shuts Shiva and her out of his yajna as the skull-bearer's wife, her own anger and her own vow leave her no road back, and she gives up her body by yoga.'

no_coincidence_resolution.evidence: The spine says: 'Shiva comes to her because of her vrat, and the last union is won by Parvati's own tapasya after Kamadeva's arrow has turned to ash.'

ending_reuses_emotional_anchor.evidence: The spine says: 'Parvati keeps the same vigil, alone and without any arrow, and this time she answers Shiva herself.'

non_flat_antagonistic_pressure.evidence: The spine says Daksha 'did hard tapasya to have her as his daughter and gave her to Shiva with joy, but pride in ritual purity turns him against the son-in-law who carries skulls.'

dialogue_shows_relationship_change.evidence: The spine says: 'Daksha's words turn from My daughter is meant for Shiva alone to He carries skulls; he has no place at my yajna.'

episodes.title: The Boon She Could Not Say
